**Finding: Compliant** (meets the preferred position — no redline proposed).

**What I checked and why:**

| Location | Assessment |
|---|---|
| §2.1–2.4 Grant of Rights (p0030, p0033–p0035) | All licences to Corio are expressly **"nonexclusive"** and run *in our favour*. No obligation for Corio to host only Commerce One software. |
| §2.4 Distribution License (p0035) | Actually **benefits us**: Commerce One may not contact Corio Customers for non-ASP licence sales and must refer inbound Customers to Corio. Not flagged. |
| §2.7 Restrictions (p0042) | Limited to copying/reverse-engineering the Software — an IP-scope restriction, not an exclusive-dealing or requirements covenant. |
| §1.3 CORIO MARKET SEGMENT / §1.11 Territory | Scope limits on customer size and geography (North America), not a covenant preventing us from sourcing procurement functionality elsewhere. §1.3 preserves our right to keep supporting customers that outgrow the threshold. |
| §13 Shared Resources | Commerce One supplies personnel to us; no reciprocal exclusivity. |
| Exhibit D, Sales & Marketing Cooperation (p0198) | Opens with *"The parties agree to the following **non-binding** sales and marketing cooperation efforts"* — so the cross-sell incentives, joint marketing plans and marketing fund create no enforceable soft exclusivity. |
| Exhibit B Revenue Sharing (p0155–p0161) | Revenue-share percentages only; no minimum purchase or all-requirements commitment. |

Searches for "exclusiv*", "compet*", "preferred", "sole supplier" and "third party" surfaced only (a) non-exclusive grants to us, (b) tax language, (c) Commerce One's ownership warranty, (d) our sole-and-exclusive *remedies* wording, and (e) the entire-agreement clause — none of which is an exclusivity obligation on the customer.

Corio therefore retains full freedom to buy from other suppliers, satisfying the playbook's preferred position. No action required on this rule.
